claims.claim: The rebuilt kai.exe (mtime 2026-10-04 23:23:02 +0100) carries the MCP integration, and its compiled core source matches the repository tree.
claims.basis: npx tauri build exited 0 and printed 'Built application at: ...kai.exe'; the bundle was stamped 2159637957e7ed09; a read-only recompute of the source hash (same shared implementation) returns 2159637957e7ed09 against the current tree; the shipped app/target/release/core/mcp/capability.js contains the measured probe branch and runtime.js contains installMcpCapability/dispatchMcpCapability; live GET /identity reports identityMatchesDisk true, freshness fresh.

claims.claim: GET /mcp is mounted on the live rebuilt app and returns 200 with the MCP summary. The 404 unknown_route symptom is dead.
claims.basis: raw live capture 2026-10-04T22:24:00Z against pid 4440 (embedded): HTTP/1.1 200 OK; body carries service 'mcp', the measured capability detail, counts, the 8 management tool ids, persistence and provenance summary. BEFORE was HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found {"error":"not_found","reason":"unknown_route","path":"/mcp"}.

claims.claim: The mcp capability health is probe-backed: with zero servers registered it measures UNAVAILABLE with the probe's branch-1 detail, not the old declared string; the status block is recomputed per call.
claims.basis: BEFORE status.detail was the declared string 'no MCP server is configured or connected' (equal to the registration-time requirements[0]); AFTER status.detail is 'no MCP server is registered; register one (POST /mcp/servers) to give KAI MCP tools', which is verbatim branch 1 of mcpCapabilityHealth (core/src/mcp/capability.ts:61-65; shipped in app/target/release/core/mcp/capability.js); checkedAt advanced 22:24:00.635Z -> 22:27:31.417Z across two calls. The requirements[] array still carries the static registration string by design — the STATUS is the measured value.

claims.claim: The probe is state-driven: it walks UNAVAILABLE -> DEGRADED -> AVAILABLE as a server is registered, enabled and connected.
claims.basis: core/tests/mcp-runtime-e2e.test.ts on this tree: real tool registry, policy engine, approval service, manager and the real fixture child process over stdio; asserts UNAVAILABLE ('registered but not enabled'), DEGRADED ('enabled but not connected'), AVAILABLE ('1 MCP server(s) connected; ... tools'). Not walked live in this row (see N1).

claims.claim: The MCP management surface is live on the one tool registry: 8 mcp.* tools registered, none refused; a management call parks 409 for approval under the default policy — no bypass path.
claims.basis: live GET /mcp shows managementTools.registered = [mcp.register, mcp.update, mcp.enable, mcp.disable, mcp.remove, mcp.connect, mcp.disconnect, mcp.refresh], refused []; the e2e test drives register/enable/connect to 409 {approvalRequired, approvalId} and executes only after a decision; policies/gate.ts maps WRITE/EXTERNAL/DESTRUCTIVE to needs_approval and no mcp.* id is in KAI_INTERNAL_STATE_TOOLS (runtime.ts).

claims.claim: GET /mcp/provenance serves the invocation ledger; with zero invocations it is empty.
claims.basis: live capture: HTTP/1.1 200 OK, {"records": []}. The e2e test asserts recorded rows (toolId, caller source, approvalId correlation) after real invocations.

The mcp capability is probe-backed and honestly measures UNAVAILABLE with zero servers registered (a measured detail, not the old declared string).
